1

Details

This note is the visual companion of <out>/capsule_pose/report.html (capsule_pose.py, make_capsule_pose_report.py). Everything uses the post-access runs, chambers A and C on the is2_v2 chain at the capsule-focus k, with stage-3 y mirrored on load (stage 3 stores y upside down; COORDINATES.md).

An earlier version of the analysis called the source "the beam at x −10.3". That was retracted: the source is where the neutrons that illuminate the capsule are captured on aluminium, and it is the beam position only if the beam is the illumination and actually hits the capsule. The slides show why the two readings on the right both survive.

The station, the capsule and the measured source, to scale

Hover the chambers, the capsule, the beam and the star. Dotted words and points everywhere carry tooltips.

geometry: run_config.json (survey), DetectorConstruction.cc polycones · beam: lamda2DvsEn_EAR2.root × fluxEAR2-Ph3

2

Details

Frame. +y is the beam, vertical and up; +z points right (A), +x up (D) in this top-down view (COORDINATES.md). The origin is the surveyed station centre, which is also where the capsule is drawn (Geant4) and what the beam was aligned to. Each chamber's strip plane is 234.6 mm (A, C) or 234.1 mm (B, D) out and is shifted 15.5–17.3 mm sideways (the "pinwheel"), so no chamber is centred on the axis.

Capsule. The STEP polycones from MX17_Full_Geant: a 0.6 mm Al barrel (OD 21.2 mm) around 500 bar ³He, a 5.5 mm thick Al nose at the bottom (upstream), a 0.9 mm CFRP wrap. Beam neutrons that reach the ³He are absorbed within ~0.15 mm, so the gas is black: Al captures (the 7.7 MeV γ that make the tracks) happen where the beam first meets Al, before the gas.

Beam. The late-window Lambda2D profile (EAR2 Phase-3 flux × the n_TOF transport radial profile per energy, as the Geant4 gun samples it): 50 % inside r = 2.0 mm, 90 % inside 7 mm, 99 % inside 18 mm.

The star is the measured source: x from chambers A and C, z from B and D, height from the y band crossing (scale-free; stage-3 y mirrored back).

Tracks from A and C converge ~10 mm toward B, not on the centre

left: real lines from A and C in the top-down view · right: their crossing points against a no-pointing null

is2_v2 cf, post-access runs, gated & angle-calibrated tracks · capsule_pose.load_data

3

Details

Each line is one reconstructed track (gated, angle-calibrated, |tan| < 0.6, ≥ 20 ms), drawn from its chamber's strip plane through the axis plane z = 0 and a little beyond. Individual lines miss the source by ~25–40 mm: the γ converts or Compton-scatters in the capsule wall and air, and the electron scatters (Geant4: p·β·θ ≈ 0.4 MeV·rad). The ensemble still focuses, and the focus is the measurement.

Two estimators, same answer. The band crossing fits displacement-to-the-axis against position on the plane and takes the zero; it is scale-free (a wrong angle scale changes the slope, not the zero). The pointing excess (right) is the histogram of crossing points minus the same tracks with shuffled angles, which keeps the acceptance and destroys pointing; its peak survives background that ruins the band crossing before ~10 ms.

Chamber A's u axis points along +x and C's along −x, yet both find −10. A shift, a tan bias or a twist of one chamber would move the two images in opposite directions.

The pointing image is one compact spot left of the frame centre, at all times

chamber A, lines at the axis plane minus the shuffled-angle null, normalised per panel; white: the capsule as drawn

capsule_pose image.csv (A); heights mirrored back to +y = up

4

Details

Per window, a 2D histogram of where each line crosses the axis plane (x, height) minus the same with the x and y angles shuffled together among the tracks. The spot is elongated vertically because individual lines miss by ±25–40 mm in height (electron scattering, and the y angle scale is not calibrated); its centre is what the crossing estimators measure.

What is not there: a vertical ridge at the beam's x from captures along the beam line (¹⁴N(n,γ) in the air column gives 10.8 MeV γ at roughly the Al nose's rate per neutron), and a second spot near x = 0. Chamber C looks the same (image.csv).

It does not move: the same x from 2 to 75 ms, and in every run

left: pointing-excess peak per ToF bin (band crossing unusable < 10 ms) · right: per-run crossings

capsule_pose early.csv · imaging_campaign per_run.csv

5

Details

Left. The excess peak is read with gain 1 on a point source (toy: −5 → −4.7, −10 → −9.7). Mixing the late data with a copy of itself moved +10 mm shifts it by 1.0 mm × fraction × 10, linearly (the grey lines). Diluting the late data with 1–2 ms tracks (mostly background) moves it by ≤ 2 mm. A beam centred on the frame with the capsule partly in it would put its own captures near x ≈ 0: at 2σ, at most 34 % (A) / 10 % (C) of the capsule tracks at 4–6 ms and 5 % at 6–12 ms come from there. A at 4–6 ms is the only bin that moves, and C in the same bin does not, so it is more likely background structure.

Right. The campaign-imaging crossings per run (production chain): post-access A -8.3 (s.d. 0.3), C -10.3 (0.5), D -3.5; pre-access A -9.5, C -10.3. The access did not move it. The production chain reads A ~2 mm closer to 0 than is2_v2; C agrees between chains.

Where the neutrons are captured decides where the source appears

side views, capsule at drawn height; gold: beam; dots: Al captures; stars: predicted (colour) vs measured (red)

6

Details

A ray walks up through the capsule: in Al it is captured with probability Σ ds (0.8 % through the 5.5 mm nose), neutron scattering in the CFRP and Al takes it off its path, and if it reaches the ³He it is gone. The capture point is therefore where the beam first meets Al.

1. Beam on the capsule axis: almost every capture is in the nose, so the source sits at the nose and at the beam's x. Moved to x −10.3 here, it lands on the measured star.

2. Beam centred as aligned, capsule 10 mm off: the core grazes the barrel wall, which it runs along for ~40 mm (5 % capture per ray), so the captures climb the wall at the beam's x. Predicted source: x ≈ −1, height ≈ −8.

3. Capsule far enough off that only the beam's tail reaches it: the near-side wall is lit, so the source x can reach −10, but it sits on the barrel (height ≈ −12) and only ~1 % of the beam reaches the ³He.

The stars are not the centroid of the dots: they are the chambers' band crossings on Geant4 tracks translated to these capture points, which is what the data are compared with.

With the beam as aligned, nothing reaches the data at drawn height

predicted source (x, height) for each picture, against chambers A and C

Only the black curve reaches the data at the drawn height. It is the beam on the capsule; moved to x −10 it needs the capsule just 4 mm lower.

Purple / orange: beam centred as aligned, capsule 10 or 13 mm off, flux ×1…×10 the Lambda2D width. To reach x −10 the flux must be ×10 wider, and the source is still ~14 mm too high.

Grey: capsule 15–20 mm off, lit by the tail: x −10 at 17.5 mm off, 20 mm too high, and ~1 % of the beam on the ³He.

A capsule-height change moves a point straight down: the height is degenerate with how much barrel is lit; the x is not.

capsule_pose alternatives.csv + halo.csv (late window, A/C mean)

7

Details

Each curve is one picture with the flux width scaled from the Lambda2D profile (×1, 2, 3, 5, 10), computed by the full model (ray trace + Geant4 tracks + the data's estimators); hover the points for the ³He share and the height change each needs. The black curve is computed on the frame centre and moved sideways to the data's x, which is legitimate because the model is translation-equivariant (closure: a +5 mm shift reads +4.9).

The data stars sit 2–6 mm below the black ×1 point. The capsule's height in the chamber frame has never been measured, so a few mm is unremarkable; 14–25 mm (what every other picture needs) would be a mounting error.

Not in the grid: tilts. They were scanned for the beam-on-capsule family (0–20°, both senses) and change the height by at most a few mm while the beam stays on the nose.

Most capsule tracks come after the beam, yet they image the same nose spot

left: arrival time of capsule-pointing tracks vs expected beam captures · right: source height vs ToF

capsule_tof tof.csv / beam_capture.csv · capsule_pose tof.csv

8

Details

Left. 87 % of the beam's own captures (EAR2 flux × 1/v) fall before 12 ms, peaking at 5–6 ms; 92 % of the tracks that point at the capsule are after 12 ms and half after 30 ms (recorded rates, DAQ-limited, so only the shape means anything). The ≥ 30 ms trigger rate falls with T½ ≈ 24 ms, read in the tracking handoff (§10f) as the die-away of thermalised neutrons in the EAR2 hall.

Right. Those late tracks image the nose (−31 / −35) and the same x. An isotropic hall flux would light the whole capsule body and put the source at y ≈ +5 to +8. So whatever illuminates the capsule late is narrow and on the nose, like a beam, which is not understood; it is also why the direct-beam test cannot isolate the beam: the 4–12 ms capsule tracks are a mixture whose beam share is unknown.

Before 12 ms the height drops; that follows the purity drop and no pose moves the beam window down, so it is read as an unsubtracted beam-line source below the capsule.

A misplaced chamber cannot fake this: it would split A and C

the A and C x views point opposite ways in global x

A and C agree (-10.1 / -10.7 mm), so the offset is not a strip-map, angle or alignment error of one chamber. The same holds for B and D in z (−4.1 / −3.5).

What survives is a shift of the whole A–C pair (and B–D pair) against the beam. That is exactly the beam-vs-frame question.

The scintillators cannot test it: the SiPM wall sits within 1–6 mm of the survey, but wall and chambers share one structure.

The x sign was fixed by this same split (2026-08-20): a wrong sign splits A and C by twice the ~16 mm pinwheel.

9

Details

U_HAT is +x for A and −x for C (ntof_tracking/reco/geometry.py). Any error that lives in a chamber's own coordinates — the strip-map centre (STRIP_MAP_HALF), a constant tan offset, a yaw about y, or a sign — therefore moves the two images in opposite global directions. Their agreement to 0.5 mm (is2_v2) bounds those to well below the 10 mm offset. The production chain reads A ~2 mm closer to 0 than is2_v2; that is the chain systematic.

The chamber centres in run_config.json are the survey's (pinwheel shifts 15.5 / 15.75 / 16.35 / 17.3 mm; MX17_Full_Geant docs/HANDOFF_ARM_GEOMETRY.md). A common shift of both A and C (A's pinwheel 10 mm smaller, C's 10 mm larger) is invisible to every internal check.

Two readings survive, and only an outside measurement separates them

top-down zooms to scale: beam (gold), capsule (outline), frame centre (+), measured source (star)

Reading 1

The beam is not where the frame says, or the frame is not where it was aligned.

³He gets ≥ 85 % of the beam (capsule within ±5 mm of drawn).

Needs one surprise: a ~10 mm beam/frame offset.

Reading 2

The beam is centred; the capsule is far off it, lower than drawn, lit by its tail or a wider beam.

³He gets 1–15 % of the beam: IPC and X17 yields cut ×7–100.

Needs two surprises: the offset and a ≥ 14 mm drop.

10

Details

What would decide it: how the beam centring was done and against what (laser on the beam axis? the capsule holder? the frame?); a survey or photo of the capsule against the beam axis; the capsule tip's height against the chamber mid-plane and how the capsule is held (anything massive near the nose would also explain why late, non-beam neutrons image the nose); the beam spot at the station (collimator in use, distance from the 19.5 m point, halo beyond Lambda2D's 3 cm).

What the data already exclude: a Lambda2D beam at the frame centre hitting the capsule anywhere at its drawn height; a source at x ≈ 0 making more than ~5 % of the capsule tracks after 6 ms; a single misplaced or twisted chamber (A and C would disagree).

Neither reading explains the 1 : 8 same-chamber pair rate on its own: in reading 1 the Al capture rate per neutron is near nominal; in reading 2 it falls, but so does everything the capsule makes.

What this does not rule out, and what would settle it

not ruled out

  • The beam and the frame ~10 mm apart (reading 1), or the capsule far off a centred beam and well below its drawn height (reading 2).
  • A source that is not the capsule Al: a holder or fitting at the nose, lit by the hall flux.
  • A beam spot unlike Lambda2D at the station: distance, collimator, halo beyond 3 cm.
  • Why the after-the-flux population images the nose like a beam, not the whole capsule.
  • A ~3.6σ hint of a second, higher source (x-vs-height step), Geant4-library-limited.

questions for the hardware

  1. How was the beam centred, and against what? Was it checked against the capsule?
  2. Capsule tip height against the chamber mid-plane, and how the capsule is held.
  3. The beam spot at the station (n_TOF profile measurement, collimator in use).
  4. A photo or survey of the capsule against the beam axis settles both readings at once.
